P: 1. Assess hydration and ability to tolerate oral rehydration; consider BMP when dehydration is significant and targeted stool testing for severe, persistent or bloody illness rather than routinely; educate about oral rehydration, hand hygiene and warning signs; recheck within 24–48 hours and use urgent care for inability to drink, scant urine, bloody stool or worsening focal pain. 2. Ask about recurrent episodes, nocturnal diarrhea, weight loss and blood; pursue stool inflammatory testing and gastroenterology evaluation only if persistent features support it; explain that current acute exposure makes infection more likely.

3.
